CakePHP and Slim apps onto Laravel#

This page covers cakephp-to-laravel and slim-to-laravel, the two faces of one hop that moves a CakePHP or Slim app onto Laravel 13 without a rewrite. Before this: CakePHP and Slim apps to PHP 8.5. Next: Strict session IDs for raw PHP apps.

CakePHP and Slim are being phased out at WSU (D-124). The upgrade hops keep an app supported; this hop retires the framework. It is the strangler fig pattern: Laravel grows around the old app, one route or form at a time, until nothing is left to strangle. The old app keeps answering every request it has not handed over yet, so the app ships after every run, not after a big-bang rewrite.

Before you start#

The hop is opt-in, and it is always the last step of a plan. It needs:

  • The framework's latest major. CakePHP 5 or Slim 4. Run the upgrade hops first (booster plan shows them).
  • PHP 8.3 or newer. SESAME and Laravel 13 both need it.
  • A committed, clean tree. The mount moves the whole app, so --allow-dirty does not apply to this hop.
  • A usable replay. booster-replay.json with no todo items left, and a baseline that is not one redirect everywhere or all errors. Draft it with booster replay init; the replay gate has the details. The replay is the only thing that can say a moved page still answers the same, so there is no strangler without it.
  • No LTI. SESAME has no LTI driver yet, so an LTI tool's Laravel half could not sign anyone in.
booster plan --path=../my-app --to-laravel

A bare --to-laravel (no major) is the opt-in; --to-laravel=13 still only sets a Laravel app's target. --only slim-to-laravel (or cakephp-to-laravel) plans the hop alone.

Run 1: Step 0 and the mount#

booster run --path=../my-app --only slim-to-laravel --replay

Run 1 does two things and stops:

  1. Step 0, sign-in on SESAME. The old app's sign-in moves onto SESAME first, so both halves can share one sign-in and one logout. It is gated by the replay as the app is served today; the sign-in hand-off now goes to CAS, and the gate accepts exactly that change on the paths Step 0 names. An app that already signs in through SESAME skips the change. Both halves require waynestate/sesame ^0.10.1: 0.10.0 lost the signed-in identity on Laravel's JSON sessions, so a logout on one half did not end the other. On a Laravel app with JSON sessions, users signed in under 0.10.0 are signed out once after the upgrade and sign in again (usually silently, through SSO).
  2. The mount. Laravel 13 goes at the app root (the same app sourdough new --laravel makes). The old Composer root moves, unchanged, to legacy/ with its own vendor/. public/index.php becomes a small dispatcher that sends every request to legacy unless the route table, bootstrap/booster-moved.php, says Laravel has it. The Laravel half signs in under /_laravel/login. The replay checks the mounted app against the untouched app's answers (--serve-changed, since the app is now served another way). The root composer.json lists the old app's Composer repositories too (a relative path or artifact repository now points into legacy/), so both halves find the same packages.

Only when the mount passes its gate does Booster write the ledger, booster-strangler.json. A mount that fails leaves its changes in place for you to read, and no ledger: undo it with git checkout -- . && git clean -fd and run again once the cause is fixed.

Commit run 1, then deploy it together with the one Citadel change it needs: the app's public directory becomes public (the report lists it under MANUAL).

Later runs: one unit at a time#

booster run --path=../my-app --only slim-to-laravel --replay --moves 1
booster run --path=../my-app --only slim-to-laravel --replay --route "GET /users/{id}"

A unit is one route, or one form (its GET and its POST move together). The ledger lists every unit with its state: legacy, laravel (Booster moved it), hand (a person ported it) or failed (it failed a gate). Units move in a set order: stateless pages first, then pages, then writes, then the ones that need sign-in.

--moves N moves the next N units still in legacy (1 by default); --route "<id>" moves just that one, and is also how to retry a failed unit. Booster writes the Laravel route and controller, adds the unit to the route table, and (when the move added a package to the Laravel half's composer.json) runs composer update -W for it in the gate image; a failed update marks the unit failed with Composer's first error line and the run stops before the gate. Then it runs the gate with the moved units answering from Laravel: the syntax check over both halves, the old app's own tests from inside legacy/, then the replay. A green run marks the units laravel. A red one marks them failed, leaves the changes in place, and says how to undo them. A failed unit waits for a person: the next --moves run skips it.

Each run is one diff to review and commit. Booster never commits.

A moved route keeps the old answer's headers. The first move sets HELMET's scope to web in config/helmet.php, and every moved route skips HELMET's SecurityHeaders, InjectRibbon and RequestForgeryGuard, so a moved page carries no CSP or X-Frame-Options the old app did not send (a nonce CSP would also block its inline scripts). The Laravel half's own pages keep all three. A MANUAL line says so; once the units are on Laravel, drop the skips one route at a time and check each page under HELMET's CSP. A hand-ported route needs the same skip until then.

When a package a move or Step 0 adds needs a shared package (such as psr/http-message 2) that a locked package holds at its old major, the gate's composer update -W fails on it; Booster then names those locked packages once more, inside composer.json's constraints, and says which in the report.

A moved CakePHP unit that reads the database uses the old app's own connection. At request time, inside the Laravel process, CakeDatabase reads the default Datasource from legacy/config/app.php and legacy/config/app_local.php and opens it as the Laravel connection cake. That is the app reading its own config, the way the old half does on every request. Booster never reads those values when it moves a unit, and they never reach a report or a log. When the Laravel half gets its own DB_* settings, point the moved models at them and drop the bridge (a MANUAL line says so).

After Step 0 on an app with a form sign-in, src/Sesame/UserResolver.php looks up the row the form used to find (for example Users by email) by the CAS username, so getIdentifier() still returns that row's id and policies and user_id writes keep working. A person with no row signs in with a username only and no id. Make sure that field holds what CAS sends (the AccessID). The mount gives the Laravel half's resolver, app/Sesame/StranglerUserResolver.php, the same lookup on the legacy database, once a moved unit has brought CakeDatabase, so a moved page sees the same id as the legacy one.

A unit Booster cannot move#

When a unit uses something Booster cannot translate exactly, it refuses that unit, names the file and line, and moves on to the next one. Port it by hand in the Laravel half (routes/web.php and a controller), then flip it:

booster run --path=../my-app --only slim-to-laravel --replay --hand --route "FORM /articles/add"

Booster checks that php artisan route:list has every method of the unit at its URI, adds it to the route table, marks it hand and gates it like any other move.

Finish#

booster run --path=../my-app --only slim-to-laravel --replay --finish

Once no unit is left in legacy, --finish deletes legacy/, the route table and the install hook, puts back Laravel's stock public/index.php, moves /login to Laravel, and gates the result against the replay (--serve-changed). When it passes, the ledger goes too: the app is a plain Laravel app, and the next booster plan plans it like one. While units are left, --finish refuses and lists them.

--finish also refuses, naming the units, while moved Slim code still needs the old app at run time: a Slim-hosted unit (it runs a copy of the legacy front controller inside its Laravel route), or an app whose moved units run in container app mode (the copied legacy setup boots per request for its services and app-wide middleware). Port those services to a Laravel provider and that middleware to Laravel middleware first.

Before legacy/ goes, the old docroot's static files (robots.txt, images, css) are copied into public/, where the dispatcher served them from; a file public/ already has with other content is a MANUAL line. When the finish gate still fails with every unit on Laravel, the difference is usually the old app's own fallback: what it answered for paths no unit owns (its not-found or method-not-allowed page) and for a trailing-slash path Laravel matches as the route without it. Port that to Laravel (Route::fallback(), the exception handler) and run --finish again.

While the move is in progress#

An app with a ledger plans only the strangler: every other hop waits for --finish, and the plan says so. To patch the old app meanwhile (a security fix, a PHP hop), run Booster on it alone with --path=../my-app/legacy.

The report#

Every strangler run reports, in text and in the JSON report's strangler section:

  • the units moved this run, each with its replay line;
  • the units still in legacy, with failed ones marked;
  • every refusal, with file and line; a refusal several units share prints once with the units it names, and when every refused unit runs the same file (a CakePHP base controller's initialize()), a MANUAL line says to port that file first;
  • the MANUAL checklist, grouped: sign-in, mount, route moves, finish;
  • for Slim, the Slim-hosted units still in routes/web.php and their SLIM-HOSTED: lines, in their own section (strangler.slim_hosted in JSON);
  • the next command to run.

Stop signs#

Each one means nothing changed: not on the framework's latest major, PHP under 8.3, a dirty tree, legacy/ there without a ledger (a mount that did not pass), a Laravel app already at the root (artisan, bootstrap/app.php or routes/web.php), no usable replay, and an LTI app. A Slim skeleton's own app/ folder is not one: it moves into legacy/ with the rest of the old app.
